key_insight: KV-streams proposes a plug-and-play way to compact long agent traces without repeatedly re-prefilling the entire LLM context. This keeps memory use stable while making trainable compaction much more efficient for agentic reinforcement learning.
problem_solved: Agentic LLMs need to maintain very long interaction traces, which quickly exhaust GPU memory. Existing context-compaction methods reduce memory use, but they often require repeated full-context prefilling, which slows training and hurts throughput.
method: Introduce KV-streams as a compacting mechanism that reuses and streams key/value cache information efficiently.
Design the method to be plug-and-play, so it can integrate with existing agentic RL and LLM training pipelines with minimal changes.
Avoid repeated full-context prefilling during compaction, reducing compute overhead while preserving long-horizon context handling.
impact: This matters because it makes long-context agent training more practical on real hardware budgets. For practitioners, it can improve throughput, lower training cost, and enable longer-horizon agentic workflows without constant memory scaling.

paper_title: KV-streams for Efficient Compaction in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Emiliano Penaloza, Dane Malenfant, Dheeraj Vattikonda, Roger Creus Castanyer, Siddarth Venkatraman
